classifications.rationale: FocusTrace reports active area elements that omit alt as an HTML content-model warning, but it does not treat aria-label or aria-labelledby as alternative naming mechanisms for that structural check, so the expectations overlap without being equivalent.

FocusTrace checks whether known ARIA states and properties are supported by the resolved role and includes normalized ElementInternals role/property evidence when the MAIN-world bridge captured it. Its WAI-ARIA 1.3 authoring-warning model and axe applicability/exceptions are still not identical.

FocusTrace reviews non-empty braille labels and braille role descriptions for observable non-braille accessible-name or aria-roledescription counterparts. It deliberately keeps SHOULD-level and user-agent-dependent authoring expectations as REVIEW rather than asserting axe-equivalent deterministic failure semantics.

FocusTrace deterministically names buttons and links and applies those checks to captured ElementInternals-only command roles, but it still does not provide one equivalent rule for every axe command role such as all menuitem variants.

FocusTrace now detects bounded conditional ARIA misuse including treegrid-only row properties outside treegrid context and native checkbox/radio state conflicts. The implementation intentionally does not claim axe's complete conditional-attribute matrix.
FocusTrace explicitly reports use of deprecated ARIA roles from its synchronized ARIA registry; this is materially the same authoring expectation.

FocusTrace deterministically fails a top-level document body that declares aria-hidden=true and keeps the check inapplicable to component roots, materially matching the benchmark condition while citing ARIA in HTML and WCAG directly.
FocusTrace implements the sequential-focus subset with explicit evidence, while broader focusability/tree edge cases remain outside its current bounded expectation.

FocusTrace checks accessible names for its supported form-field and input-role set, including captured ElementInternals-only roles and form-associated labels, but not every specialized ARIA input applicability path covered by axe.

FocusTrace checks exposed native meter, explicit role=meter and captured ElementInternals role=meter semantics for a non-empty accessible name while retaining a deliberately bounded local AccName implementation.

FocusTrace checks exposed native progress, explicit role=progressbar and captured ElementInternals role=progressbar semantics for a non-empty accessible name while retaining a deliberately bounded local AccName implementation.
FocusTrace reports ARIA states/properties prohibited for the resolved role, but it uses the current ARIA authoring registry and warning semantics rather than axe's exact rule contract.

FocusTrace checks required states/properties for resolved ARIA roles and accepts captured ElementInternals reflections as observable required-state evidence. Registry version, implicit-role handling and outcome semantics still differ from axe.

FocusTrace now derives allowed accessibility child roles directly from the synchronized WAI-ARIA 1.3 role model and reports incompatible semantic children after aria-owns ownership is resolved. It deliberately does not invent a missing-child failure where the current normative allowed-child wording does not require a child to be present, so the relationship is overlap rather than equivalent.

FocusTrace now derives required accessibility-parent roles directly from the synchronized WAI-ARIA 1.3 role model and resolves transparent wrappers plus valid aria-owns ownership. Outcome and repair boundaries remain intentionally conservative, so it is still classified as overlap.
